prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your ZIP code, budget, the size/age of your home, whether ducts need work, and whether you want a particular brand or high-efficiency system. I can help you pick the best contractor for your situation if you tell me your ZIP code and a few details. Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and checklist so you can find a great Atlanta contractor.

What to do
- Get at least 3 written estimates from different reputable contractors.
- Require a Manual J load calculation (not a rule-of-thumb) — this determines the correct system size.
- Compare by model numbers and SEER ratings (don’t just compare total price).
- Confirm the contractor will pull permits and arrange inspections if required.

How to vet companies (must-haves)
- Proper licensing and insurance for Georgia (ask for license number and proof of liability insurance).
- NATE-certified or factory-trained technicians.
- Written contract with equipment model, serial numbers, efficiency (SEER), estimated performance, labor warranty, and timeline.
- Clear warranty: manufacturer warranty plus a labor/installation warranty (ask length and transferability).
- Good local reviews and at least a few recent references. Check Google, BBB, Angi, Yelp, and local Facebook groups.
- No-pressure sales and clear answers about ductwork, refrigerant, airflow, and startup testing.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calc and provide the results?
- What brand and exact model are you recommending, and why?
- What is included in the scope (new pad, disconnect, line set, thermostat, condenser coil protection, cleanup)?
- How long will installation take and who performs the work (company employees or subs)?
- What are the total out-the-door costs, permit fees, and any rebates available?
- What warranty is included on labor and parts?

Typical price expectations (very approximate)
- Basic replacement (existing ductwork, mid-efficiency 13–16 SEER): expect roughly $3,000–$7,000.
- High-efficiency systems (17+ SEER, new equipment, or duct upgrades): $6,000–$12,000+.
Prices vary by home size, access, needed ductwork, and brand.

Local resources and rebates
- Check Georgia Power, local utility programs, and manufacturer rebates for incentives on high-efficiency systems.
- Use Google Reviews, BBB, and local Facebook groups for recent customer experiences.

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short list of top-rated Atlanta HVAC contractors near you (tell me your ZIP).
- Help prepare a comparison checklist you can give to each contractor.
- Explain specific brands and SEER levels if you have a preference.

Which would you like to do next?
